title: Keep directions, account for repetition
subtitle: Dobb · Design-editing post-training · Alignment scaling · Data-constrained training
intro: Two main readings and one brief, catching up on October 29 releases: complete directions within shards, multidimensional editing evaluation, and limits of alignment extrapolation. The classic examines effective sample size under repetition.

articles.paper: Dobb: Shard-Local Preconditioning in Block-Diagonal Eigenbases
articles.authors: Shi-Yuk Fong · Shuhua Yu · Jiawei Zhang
articles.title: Partition blocks without truncating directions

blocks.text: Muon’s whole-matrix operations conflict with sharding. Dobb drops cross-block activation correlations, retains a complete orthonormal basis U per block, and applies elementwise signs to projected momentum M.[1]

blocks.label: Paper update; m is the full output dimension; bases refresh periodically [1]
With complete orthonormal bases and nonzero coefficients; singular values need not be equal [1]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Learning rate and weight decay follow a shared protocol. Pooled timing shares a forward–backward estimate; it is not full-training wall time. Blocks must fit within shards; moments still require data-parallel synchronization. The 13.5× optimizer-call ratio is not end-to-end speedup.[1]

blocks.text: Teachers generate starting-design/request/successful-edit triples. Deterministic validators and visual judges filter candidates; feedback repairs edits. An early Llama 3.3 70B used over 250,000 examples; later work adds other bases and RL.[2]

blocks.label: Explanatory notation: several evaluation dimensions, not a disclosed reward formula

blocks.text: Structural checks, visual assessment and designer calibration provide separate evidence. SFT teaches native file syntax, but the authors report generalization limits. RL algorithms and reward weights are undisclosed.[2]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Speed, undo rates and ratings reflect changes across the whole agent, including tools and harness. They do not isolate RL or the editing model’s contribution.[2]

classic.question: If repetition-decay constants differ across domains, which domain deserves more unique data rather than more repetitions under fixed compute?

blocks.text: Chinchilla (2022) balances parameters and tokens while treating new tokens alike. Here unique data are limited: U_D counts unique tokens, R_D additional passes, and all D presentations cost compute.[4,5]

blocks.label: N counts parameters; positive coefficients are fitted, not a universal theorem [4]
Paper effective-data model; R_D* is a fitted decay scale [4]
U_N is the smaller of N and the Chinchilla-optimal size for the unique data [4]
Explanatory differentiation: fixed U_D and decay scale; marginal value falls
Explanatory chain rule: N′ stays fixed with N; this is not joint optimal allocation

blocks.text: GPT-2/C4 experiments vary size, unique data and passes, with cosine schedules matched to run length. A few passes nearly match fresh data; longer repetition saturates. This does not imply that training becomes useless immediately after four passes.[4]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Saturation is a fitted-model prediction, not an information-theoretic impossibility. Quality, schedules and architecture require revalidation; the law does not transfer directly to RL rollouts.[4]
